ratings_why.fun: Watching the Burrow count climb and then pour out through Onward is a clear, satisfying arc, and most cards read in one line.
ratings_why.distinct: An off-board reserve that is fight HP, currency and missiles at once plays unlike any of today's tribes or a plain token tribe.

verdict_why: The core reads well; two cards need their wording pinned down (who the front unit is, and what Identical Cousin picks).

points.text: "Your front unit" is never defined, here or on Brother Onward. Say it is your first unit in reading order (so a back-row unit leads once the front row is empty), or name F1.
Identical Cousin doesn't say who picks the Kit or the unit to copy when several are next to it. Write "Choose a Kit next to this and another unit next to this" and say what "plain" keeps.
The Burrow is the tribe's whole story but lives off the board. Show it as a snow-hall strip on the hero with a count both players see, ticking down as Kits come out.
The boom-and-crash theme only shows through spending. A card that pays for letting the Herd crash on purpose (a lemming year) would carry the seed's best idea further.
Tally's text never mentions Kits, so it reads as a generic gold card. Counting Kits ("if 3 or more are Kits") would make the census fox actually count lemmings.

standouts.why: Ole the Learned makes the old myth literal: lemmings fall from the sky onto the enemy, and it reads at a glance.
Brother Onward's Banner is whoever is in front leads, shown in play, and growing on each death is easy to follow.
Old Mother Lemen's one line turns the Burrow into an endless tide of great-grandchildren.

weakest.why: Tally works for any full board and says nothing about lemmings.
Identical Cousin is the hardest card to read and its copy target is ambiguous.
Herding Council is a plain small buff that does what Ferrywife does better at Tier 6.

flags.note: "New front unit" is undefined once the front row empties.
Doesn't say who chooses the Kit and the unit to copy.
With Herald refilling the Burrow each Start of Turn, Ferrywife gives every real unit +6/+6 or more a turn.
With Gerd's Bristle, a long Onward chain could make fights slow to watch and prone to ties.
